title: Adam's Final Days and Shith
notes: Classical narrations say Adam entrusted guidance to his son Shith (Seth), whom many scholars count among the prophets.
A weak hadith mentions scrolls revealed to Shith; the scroll of light here stands for guidance passed on, not a particular book.
art: Adam and his family appear only as figures of light.
imagePrompt: The interior of a large stone and timber dwelling at dusk, lit by oil lamps and a central hearth, warm amber light and deep soft shadows, woven mats on the floor, parchment texture over everything; at the centre a seated figure of pale, soft light like late-afternoon sun; many generations of figures of light sitting in widening circles and spilling out of the open doorway into the night, where more lights stretch across the valley; one figure of clear, steady white-gold light seated closest; a scroll made of light passing between their hands, every head lowered; a stream of soft particles rising through the roof to join the stars.

beats.say: Adam grew old, and his children's children filled the valley.
Closest to him sat his son Shith.
Adam placed the guidance in Shith's hands, and every head in the room bowed.
Then Adam's light faded gently and rose to join the stars.
